=== file-001.md ===
At the Threshold

The last train sighs beyond the cedar gate.
I turn where amber windows hold their flame.
Wet leaves keep small, bright coins along the path.
The porch remembers every step by name.
My key finds warmth behind the waiting door.
Inside, the kettle gathers up its song.
The hallway smells of wool and borrowed rain.
Old shadows fold their patient hands along
The table, where a single lamp is lit.
I set my weary weather by the chair.
The house receives the night without a word.
And all the dark outside becomes kind air.

=== file-001.md ===
The Porch Light

Smoke folds softly over the lane,
I turn where maples shed their gold.
The windows bloom with honeyed rain,
and welcome warms the gathering cold.

My boots bring dusk across the floor,
the kettle hums a patient tune.
The familiar latch yields at the door,
while clouds drift past a thinning moon.

Inside, the clock resumes its chime,
and supper scents the quiet hall.
I leave the road behind in time—
home holds the evening, leaf and all.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward

The lane wears copper beneath my shoes,
Smoke gathers softly above the eaves.
I carry dusk in my coat sleeves,
And the last bright hush of the fields.

A window kindles behind the gate,
Gold spills across the familiar floor.
The kettle sings; the hallway waits,
My name is warm beside the door.

Night settles gently on the hill,
And home receives me, quiet and still.

=== file-001.md ===
The Road Back

Dusk gathers softly at the gate,
Smoke curls above the quiet lane.
Leaves turn copper beneath my feet,
And windows bloom with amber rain.

The old key warms within my hand,
A kettle hums behind the door.
I carry twilight on my coat,
Then leave it resting on the floor.

The house receives my tired breath,
Its lamps recall my childhood name.
Night closes round the sheltered rooms,
And every threshold holds a flame.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward

The last light gathers in the maple leaves,
Gold coins trembling above the quiet lane.
My shoes remember every crooked stone,
And chimney smoke unthreads the cooling rain.

A window blooms beyond the garden gate,
Its amber square a harbor through the blue.
The kettle's small and steadfast song begins;
The door swings wide, and all the rooms are true.

I bring the dusk in softly on my coat,
With wind and leaf-musk folded in its seams.
At last, the night can find me by the fire,
Returning home to warm, familiar dreams.

=== file-001.md ===
Porch Light, Wet Boots

Leaves stick blackly to my shoes.
The bus coughs away without me.
Rain has wrung the daylight thin.
I drag my coat through the gate.
The fence leans like a bad tooth.
Inside, the radiator clanks and spits.
Soup skin shivers in its bowl.
My keys scrape the wrong lock twice.
The hallway smells of damp wool.
The clock chews loudly at the wall.
I drop my bag beside the door.
Home opens its tired mouth and keeps me.

=== file-001.md ===
Porch Light, Like a Bad Tooth

The sky coughs orange into the ditch.
My shoes bring leaves in by the handful.
The screen door slaps my shoulder twice.
Wet wool follows me through the hall.
Somebody burned dinner before I got here.
The radiator ticks like a nervous bug.
I drop my keys beside last week's mail.
Outside, the trees look half-undressed.
Mud loosens its grip from my heels.
The windows sweat over the dark yard.
I call this warmth and mean it, mostly.
Then sit down hard in the old blue chair.

=== file-001.md ===
The Door Sticks

Wet leaves paste themselves to the steps.
My key grinds like a bad tooth.
The porch light coughs over the railing.
Cold wind drags a grocery bag along the curb.
Inside, the hall smells of dust and onions.
One boot leaks brown water by the mat.
The radiator knocks its bent little fist.
I drop my coat on the chair with the broken leg.
Darkness clots in the kitchen window.
The clock chews loudly through six o'clock.
I stand there, muddy, listening for nothing.
Then the old house takes me in without a word.

=== file-001.md ===
Porch Light at Dusk

Wet leaves slap the curb like old fish.
My boots bring brown water through the door.
The sky is a bruised apple over the roofs.
Smoke crawls from chimneys with nowhere nice to go.
I carry the cold in my sleeves.
The gate squeals its rusty little complaint.
A crow coughs once from the black tree.
The windows glow, greasy and yellow.
Soup breathes onion steam into the hall.
My coat drops dead on the chair.
Home smells of dust, wool, and tired hands.
Outside, autumn keeps chewing the dark.

=== file-001.md ===
# Home by Dusk

Wet leaves rot in the gutter like old teeth.
My shoes cough mud across the porch.
The sky is a bruised peach gone soft.
A crow jerks black wire through the cold.
I carry my keys like little bones.
The door sticks, swollen with rain.
Inside, the hallway smells of dust and onions.
The radiator knocks its dumb iron fist.
My coat drips brown on the floor.
Somewhere a clock chews the dark.
I shut the world outside with one hard turn.
Home squats around me, warm and ugly.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward, With Wet Shoes
The bus coughs me onto a ditch of leaves.
Streetlamps buzz like tired appliances.
My key is cold and shaped like an excuse.
Rain has pasted receipts along the curb.
The porch sags under its bucket of dark.
Inside, the radiator clicks without warmth.
I drop my bag beside yesterday's mail.
The hallway smells of wool and old onions.
One brown leaf rides in on my heel.
The window shows a sky the color of dishwater.
I lock the door; it fails to improve anything.
Autumn keeps dripping from my coat.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward, Under Bad Leaves

The bus coughs black breath at the wet curb.
I drag my shoes through leaf-sludge and wrappers.
The sky has the color of an old dishpan.
A cold rain needles the back of my neck.
Porches blink weakly behind bent hedges.
My keys scrape around like loose teeth.
The door sticks, swollen with weather.
Inside, the hallway smells of dust and cabbage.
The radiator knocks without warming anything.
I drop my bag beside a dying fern.
Dark comes early and sits in every chair.
Still, the chipped kitchen light knows my face.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward, With Wet Leaves
The bus coughs me out by the cracked curb.
Rain has made the gutters fat and brown.
My key scratches at the stiff old lock.
Cold air sits in the hall like laundry.
Boot marks smudge the floorboards black.
The radiator ticks but gives no warmth.
A pear collapses softly in its bowl.
I drag my coat across the chair's bent arm.
The window shows a street of sodden lamps.
Some leaf paste clings to my sleeve.
I eat toast standing under the buzzing light.
Night settles in the sink, unwashed.

=== file-001.md ===
Autumn Return

Wet leaves paste the driveway black.
The porch bulb hums above the rail.
My shoes leave brown commas on tile.
Cold follows in behind my coat.
The mailbox coughs one soggy bill.
Windows hold their dim yellow squares.
Soup breathes salt from the kitchen pot.
The hall clock drags its metal feet.
A branch claws once against the pane.
I drop my keys into the bowl.
The house receives me without warmth.
Night settles in the unmade rooms.

=== file-001.md ===
# The Return

Rain chews the gutters beside the porch.
My key worries the swollen lock.
The yard is a darkened dishcloth.
Leaves paste themselves to my shoes.
Inside, the hall smells of cold pipes.
One bulb blinks above the stairs.
I drop the mail on the crooked chair.
The radiator coughs but gives no heat.
A pear collapses in its bowl.
The windows hold a greasy dusk.
My coat hangs like a damp argument.
Home shuts its door behind me.

=== file-001.md ===
The Rusted Threshold

I drag my boots through leaf-soup, brown and wet,
Past gutters coughing up a bitter tune.
The porch light blinks like an infected eye,
And moths collide beneath the swollen moon.
My key tastes iron in the lock's cold mouth;
The hallway breathes of cabbage, dust, and rain.
A radiator knocks its crooked teeth,
While orange shadows clot the windowpane.
I hang the evening on a splintered nail,
Its sleeves still full of wind and chimney smoke.
Then home receives me, creaking at the seams,
A sagging jaw that opens for a ghost.

=== file-001.md ===
# Soot-Colored Doorstep

The sky coughs rust into the gutters.
I drag my shoes through a broth of leaves.
Streetlamps blink like sickly eggs.
My coat smells of rain and old pennies.
The bus exhales me beside the crooked hedge.
A crow drops a walnut onto the dark.
Windows simmer with yellow, judgmental light.
The wind stuffs cold fingers under my collar.
Home squats there, damp as a forgotten loaf.
I fumble the key through my numb, stupid hand.
Inside, the hall breathes cabbage and dust.
Still, I enter, trailing November behind me.

=== file-001.md ===
The House Swallows Me
Autumn drags its orange teeth across the lane.
I come home with rain stewing in each shoe.
The porch bulb blinks like a sickly little moon.
Dead leaves clap their damp hands at my knees.
Inside, the hallway smells of boiled dust.
My coat hangs up its cold, dripping mouth.
The clock chews loudly on the dark.
Windows sweat against the bruised-back sky.
I kick loose acorns from the mat like teeth.
The kettle shrieks, offended by my return.
In every room, the shadows wear my slippers.
Night folds the roof around me, greasy and warm.

=== file-001.md ===
# The Door Swallows Dusk

The avenue coughs up leaves like wet tongues.
My shoes drag soup through the bruised gold gutter.
Windows blink their jaundiced little eyes at me.
The sky hangs low, a torn sack of crows.
I carry the wind home in my hair, smelling of pennies.
At the porch, the pumpkin has collapsed into orange teeth.
The key shivers in the lock like a trapped beetle.
Inside, the hallway breathes old wool and onions.
Radiators clank their rusted prayers against the walls.
My coat slumps, a drowned animal, by the stairs.
Beyond the kitchen, darkness chews its stale bread.
Still, I enter, and the house closes its cold mouth.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward Through October

The dusk spat copper pennies at my shoes.
I dragged my coat through puddles thick as stew.
Bare trees scratched the sky with blackened forks.
A bus coughed smoke across the cabbage-dark.
My windows glowed like teeth in a wet mouth.
The gate complained, a rusted throat of rain.
Dead leaves clung to every step and sleeve.
The porch lamp buzzed, a jaundiced little moon.
Inside, the hall smelled warmly of old dust.
I dropped the day beside the peeling door.
Then autumn shut its muddy fist outside.
And home, at last, grew quiet round my bones.

=== file-001.md ===
Threshold in Sleet
The bus exhales me beneath a jaundiced sky.
Wet leaves clot the gutter like drowned moths.
My key tastes of metal against my thumb.
The porch light blinks, a tired yellow eye.
Inside, the hall keeps its cold breath held.
Mud stipples the mat in dark little wounds.
The radiator knocks behind its rusted grate.
Someone's onions linger, sweetly rotten.
Rain combs black water down the windowpane.
My coat slumps heavy over the chair.
The rooms receive me without recognition.
Night seals the door with its damp, blunt hand.

=== file-001.md ===
The Door Swells Shut

Rain gnaws the last leaves into the gutter,
and every window wears a dead, yellow stare.
My key resists, cold with another's fingerprints;
the lock coughs open on its rusted breath.

Inside, damp wool sours near the radiator.
The hall clock worries one uneven tooth.
Mud darkens beneath the mat like old tea,
and the ceiling keeps lowering by degrees.

I leave my coat beside the peeling wall.
The rooms receive me without a sound.
Beyond the glass, November rubs its hands.
Home closes round me, airless as a fist.

=== file-001.md ===
The House at Dusk

Wet leaves clot the steps like drowned moths.
The key turns stiffly in the swollen lock.
Inside, the hall exhales its cellar breath.
Rain ticks coldly through a cracked gutter.
My coat drips black pools across the tiles.
The radiator groans but gives no warmth.
Old cooking clings to the yellow curtains.
A fly beats itself against the windowpane.
The rooms receive me without a sound.
Darkness thickens in the unmade bed.
Beyond the glass, bare branches scrape the sky.
I close the door and hear the house settle.

=== file-001.md ===
The Porch Light Sours

Rain gums the steps with leaf-brown paste.
The key resists, cold in its lock.
Behind the door, stale rooms exhale.
My coat drips darkness on the mat.
The radiator knocks like a trapped fist.
Wind worries the loose pane upstairs.
In the sink, a cup wears yesterday's skin.
The hallway bulb blinks, then bruises dim.
Wet shoes leave little graves of mud.
No window offers anything but black glass.
I carry the evening in on my sleeves.
Home closes around me, damp and close.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward, Late October

Rain needles the collar of my coat.
The buses cough black along the curb.
Leaves rot slickly beneath my shoes.
A crow worries a scrap in the gutter.
Windows glow, but none look welcoming.
The key turns cold against my thumb.
Inside, the hall smells of wet wool.
The radiator clicks like small teeth.
Mold shadows the corner by the stairs.
My room waits stale behind its door.
Wind rattles the pane without mercy.
Night settles in, and does not leave.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward, Beneath Rusted Leaves

The bus coughs me out beside the dented gate.
Wet leaves paste themselves to my tired shoes.
A wind worries the loose tin of the shed.
The porch light blinks like an anxious eye.
I smell coal smoke, onions, and cold wool.
My key grates loudly in the swollen lock.
Inside, the hallway keeps its puddle of dark.
A radiator rattles its small iron teeth.
The clock has dragged the evening into rain.
I hang my coat among the shadows' coats.
Then home, all crooked warmth and peeling paint,
Closes around me with its muddy hands.

=== file-001.md ===
Home by Six

The bus coughs me out beside the wet bin yard,
Leaves paste themselves to the curb like old receipts.
My shoes make a soup of the gutter's brown teeth,
And every window wears its yellow stare.
I drag the key through a pocket full of lint,
Past the fence with its one collapsed, tired panel.
The porch bulb buzzes over a dead moth's wing.
Inside, the hallway smells of damp wool and onions.
I kick off mud, miss the mat, and let it spread.
The radiator clanks its small iron complaint.
Beyond the glass, the trees shed into darkness.
I close the door; the evening follows me in.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward, Under Leaves

The bus coughs me out by the cracked curb.
Orange leaves mash darkly in the gutter.
My shoes take their wet, defeated sound ahead.
The porch bulb hums like a trapped wasp.
I drag the key through the stubborn lock.
Cold follows me in, licking the hall tiles.
The coat rack leans with everyone else's weather.
Soup-sour air sits low over the kitchen.
I find a sock beneath the radiator, stiff as bark.
Outside, rain needles the blackened hedge.
I shut the door; the house exhales dust.
At last, my name is waiting on the mat.

=== file-001.md ===
Home by Dusk

The bus coughs me beside the ditchy lane,
Wet leaves cling like receipts to my shoes.
My window glows a jaundiced yellow square,
And smoke makes a smudge above the roof.
The gate complains; I answer with my knee.
A pear lies split and browning on the path.
Inside, the hall has swallowed all its warmth,
My coat drips little commas on the mat.
The kettle hisses, mean as rainy wires.
I peel the darkened apple from my pocket.
Beyond the glass, November chews the trees.
I eat alone, then turn the lock behind me.

=== file-001.md ===
Mud on the Mat

The bus exhales me beside the bent-lit store,
leaves rasping brown paper down the gutter.
My key finds the lock with a cold little scrape;
the porch bulb blinks like a tired eye.
Wet leaves cling to the steps in bruised heaps,
and my shoes drag their black weather indoors.
The hall smells of radiator dust and onions.
A coat sags from its hook, damp at the cuffs.
Somewhere a pipe coughs behind the wallpaper.
I set my bag down hard beside the door.
The rooms receive me without ceremony,
while night packs the windows full of rain.
